title: FAQ, Troubleshooting and Support
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Chapter 23 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: You find **frequent questions per process phase** and **known errors by market and release**, distinguish **usage question, data deviation and incident**, compile the **information for a support case**, and know the **support and escalation paths** and **confirmed workarounds** (Chapters 23.1 to 23.6).

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: 23.1 – 23.3 Classify
bullets: Frequently asked questions by process phase
Known errors by market and release
Usage question, data deviation and incident

steps: First search the **FAQ per process phase** (23.1) and the **known errors** for your market and release (23.2).
Classify your issue (23.3):
**Usage question**: handbook and Quick Guide
**Data deviation**: leading system and business department (Chapter 16.2)
**Incident**: support case
Compile the **information for the support case** (23.4):
Reference number, VIN, market, division, role
Time, step, error message, screenshot

right.text: ~~Unconfirmed workarounds can damage contracts and data.~~ Use only the solutions documented in Chapter 23.6.

steps: Use the **support and escalation paths** (23.5): Vans service contract help via **sc-van@mercedes-benz.com**; further paths per market.
Apply only **confirmed workarounds** and check the **result** (23.6).

bullets: **All roles**: self-help via FAQ and workarounds
Reference number, market, division and role known
Handbook chapter for the process step checked
If information is incorrect, Customer Management will contact you; incorrect applications are rejected.
Ticket references help assign your issue to the right chapter (Appendix E).
Training material, videos and FAQ are available in the RetailPortal.

qa: How long after first registration can a service contract be concluded?
Up to 12 months and/or a maximum of 50,000 km, provided the vehicle has not yet had a service (exception: company and demonstration vehicles with a previous owner).
Can a service package be concluded for demonstration vehicles?
Demonstration and company vehicles count as used vehicles; only a pure maintenance package is possible for them.
Can a person other than the registered keeper conclude the contract?
No, contract holder and registered keeper must be identical.

title: Appendix A.1: Glossary and Abbreviations
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix A.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **glossary** explains the terms and **abbreviations** of the oneSCM handbook consistently, from ALICE to ZB II. This guide shows how to **use** and **cite** the glossary and submit **additions**.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Term groups
bullets: Roles: Dealer, MO, Market, HQ, KAM
Transactions: price information, quote, application, contract
Identifiers: VIN, OTR deal ID, VerSO order ID, model series

sections.head: Systems and documents
bullets: Systems: ALICE, OTR, VEGA, oneERP, NEMESIS, MPay, DATIX
Documents: ZB I, ZB II, SEPA mandate, price information
Status: application, signature, contract, invoice, payment status

steps: Look up the term in the **glossary**; entries are sorted alphabetically and name the chapter in which the term is introduced.
Distinguish **abbreviation** (e.g. MO) from **long form** (Market Operation); the handbook gives the long form at first occurrence.
Use the **term groups** (roles, transactions, identifiers, systems, documents, status) to find related terms.

right.text: ~~The term "contract holder" is not the same as "payer" or "user".~~ Roles on the contract are defined separately (Chapter 4.4); use the glossary terms exactly.

steps: Use the **glossary terms** in tickets, comments and training, not local paraphrases.
If a term is missing or a definition is contradictory, enter it in the **clarification register** (Appendix F, Chapter 16.7).

bullets: Term or abbreviation from the process context
Additions via the clarification register (Appendix F)
The glossary is part of the export and the online help (Chapter 3).
Language variants of the terms are documented per market (Chapter 20).
System abbreviations are explained in the profiles in Chapter 19.

qa: Where do I find the meaning of "MO"?
In the glossary under M: Market Operation, the role for business review and activation (Chapter 9).
May I use my own abbreviations?
In tickets and comments, please use glossary terms only; propose new terms via the clarification register.
Is the glossary also available in English?
Language variants depend on the market (Chapter 20); see the note in the glossary.
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

title: Appendix B.1: Everyday Checklists
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix B.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **everyday checklists** summarize, per process phase, the check items that must be met before the next step: from the **quote** through **application and signature** to **activation** and **contract management**.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

steps: Select the **checklist of the process phase** your transaction is in (process map, Chapter 3.4).
Work through the **check items** in order; each item refers to the chapter with the description.
Mark open items and clarify them **before** the next step, not afterwards.

right.text: ~~A completed checklist does not replace the system check.~~ Validation rules (Chapter 6.4) and MO Checks (Chapter 9) apply regardless of the checklist.

steps: For MO reviews, document the checklist result in the **check status** (Chapter 9.3).
If a check item is missing, report it via the **clarification register** (Appendix F).

bullets: **Dealer**: checklists before quote, application and signature
Reference number or transaction at hand
Checklist in the current handbook version
☐  Open items clarified before the next step
The checklists correspond to the "Checklist before completion" sections in the chapters' Quick Guides.
Checklists are supplemented with local items per market (Chapter 20).
Practical examples for the checklists are in Appendix I.1.

qa: Are the checklists binding?
They are working aids; the binding rules are the process rules of the chapters and the system checks.
Are the checklists available for printing?
Yes, Appendix B.1 is included as a print version in the handbook export (Chapter 16.5).
How are checklists updated?
With each release via the change overview (Chapter 22.4).

title: Appendix C.1: Process Diagrams
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix C.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **process diagrams** show the **process map**, the **sub-processes** from quote to contract end and the **handovers** between roles and systems. This guide explains how to **read** the diagrams and **apply** them to your transaction.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Symbols
bullets: Rectangle: process step with chapter reference
Color: role that performs the step

steps: Start with the **process map** and find the phase of your transaction.
Open the **sub-process diagram** of the phase; each step names the chapter.
Read the **handovers** on the arrows: Which status must be reached, which role takes over?

right.text: ~~Diagrams show the standard process.~~ Country and division deviations (Chapters 20 and 21) are documented only there, not in the diagram.

steps: Note the **decisions** (diamonds): special approval, MO Check and rejection lead to alternative paths.
Use the **transition modules** (T6-7 to T15-16) to move between chapters.

bullets: **All roles**: read diagrams and classify the transaction
Basic knowledge of the process map (Chapter 3.4)
☐  Phase found in the process map
The diagrams are shown in the dashboard as a click path.
Status transitions in detail are in Appendix D.
Diagrams are reviewed with each release (Chapter 22).

qa: Which diagram do I need for application creation?
Sub-process application (Chapter 6) with transition T6-7 to signature.
What do the colors mean?
The role that performs the step: Dealer, MO, Market, HQ or system.
Can I export diagrams?
Yes, via the handbook export (Chapter 16.5).

title: Appendix D.1: Role/Status/Scope Matrices
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix D.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **matrices** show which **role** may perform which action, which **status transitions** are permitted and which **scope** (market, division, dealership) applies to visibility and editing.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Matrices
bullets: Role matrix: action per role (Dealer, MO, Market, HQ)
Status matrix: permitted transitions per object (application, signature, contract)
Scope matrix: visibility per market, division and dealership

sections.head: Application
bullets: Before an action: May my role do this?
For status questions: Which transition is possible?
If visibility is missing: Does the scope match?

steps: Check in the **role matrix** whether your role may perform the desired action.
Read in the **status matrix** which transition is permitted from which status (Chapter 8.2).
Check in the **scope matrix** whether market, division and dealership of the transaction match your access (Chapter 2.4).

right.text: ~~The matrices are the binding reference for authorizations and status transitions.~~ A transition visible in the system but not documented must be reported, not used.

steps: If a permission is missing, request the role via ALICE (Chapter 2.3); if a transition is missing, a new contract or support is required.
Report deviations between matrix and system via the clarification register (Appendix F).

bullets: **All roles**: look up own permissions and status transitions
**MO/Market**: status matrix for reviews and changes
Role and scope of own access known (Chapter 2)
Current status of the transaction known
Application, signature and contract status are separate matrices (Chapter 3.8).
Scope restrictions explain why transactions are missing from the search (Chapter 3.2).
The matrices are the basis of role training (Chapter 17).

qa: Why can't I activate an application?
Activation is reserved for the MO or the system; see role matrix and Chapter 8.4.
Which transitions exist from "rejected"?
Resubmission after correction (Chapter 8.7); see status matrix.
Why can't I see contracts of another dealership?
The scope limits visibility to your dealership and market.

title: Appendix E.1: Ticket-to-Chapter Mapping
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix E.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **ticket-to-chapter mapping** links requirements, errors and clarifications (tickets) to the **handbook chapters** they affect. This lets you find the chapter for a ticket and the open tickets for a chapter.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Mapping
bullets: Ticket → chapter: Which chapters does the ticket change?
Chapter → tickets: Which tickets are open?
Status: open, in progress, implemented, rejected

sections.head: Benefit
bullets: Known errors per market and release (Chapter 23.2)

steps: Find the **ticket** in the mapping table; the row names chapter, status and release.
Conversely: find the **chapter** and check which tickets are open or in progress.
Read the **status**: Only implemented tickets are part of the functional baseline (Chapter 22.1).

right.text: ~~An open ticket does not change the valid process.~~ Until implementation and documentation, the current version of the handbook chapter applies.

steps: For a new ticket, state the **affected chapter** so that the mapping remains complete.
Before training sessions, check the chapter's open tickets (Chapter 22.3).

bullets: **All roles**: look up ticket status for a topic
The mapping is the basis of the change overview (Chapter 22.4).
Market-related tickets are also listed in Chapter 23.2.
Ticket references belong in the clarification register (Appendix F).

qa: Where do I find all tickets for Chapter 7?
In the mapping, filtered by chapter; status and release are given per row.
Who maintains the mapping?
Editorial team and HQ as part of version control (Chapter 16.6).
How do I report a new ticket?
Via the support path (Chapter 23.5), stating the chapter.

title: Appendix F.1: Sources and Clarification Register
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix F.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **source index** substantiates every handbook statement; the **clarification register** collects **contradictions, gaps and open questions** with status and owners. This guide shows how to **use** both and create **entries**.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Sources
bullets: Source type: system documentation, ticket, business decision, test

sections.head: Clarification register
bullets: Entry: chapter, statement, contradiction or gap

steps: For a statement, check the **source** in the source index and its **evidence status**.
If you find a **contradiction** or a **gap**, create an entry in the **clarification register**: chapter, statement, observation, source.
Assign the entry to the **responsible role** (Market, HQ, MO) and set the status to "open".

right.text: ~~No change to the handbook without a source.~~ Statements without confirmed evidence are marked as open and must not be used in training (Chapter 16.4).

steps: Track the **decision**; the result is adopted into the chapter and the source is updated.
Before releases, check the chapter's open entries (Chapter 22).

bullets: Source or ticket reference, if available
The register is required reading before releases and training.
Data protection: no personal data in entries (Chapter 16.1).
Ticket references link the register and the mapping (Appendix E).

qa: What is the difference between a source and a ticket?
The source substantiates a statement; the ticket describes a change or an error. Both are referenced.
Who decides a clarification?
The responsible role; for Blueprint questions, HQ (Chapter 15.4).
How long does an entry stay open?
Until the decision; open entries are reviewed before each release.

title: Appendix G.1: Figure Index and Evidence
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix G.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **figure index** lists all **screenshots and graphics** of the handbook with chapter, system, release and **evidence**. This guide shows how figures are **found**, **checked** and **newly captured**.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

steps: Find the figure in the **figure index** by number or chapter.
Check **release and date**: A figure from an older release may differ from the current screen.
Check the **evidence**: environment, anonymized data, approval.

right.text: ~~Screenshots with real customer, vehicle or bank data must not go into the handbook.~~ Use the test data catalog and redact any remaining data (Chapter 16.1).

steps: For a **new figure**: capture the screen with test data (Appendix I.3), assign chapter and release, obtain approval.
Replace outdated figures and update the index (Chapter 16.6).

bullets: **All roles**: assign figures to a chapter and release
Safe sample data in the figure (Chapter 16.1)
The Quick Guides contain process images; screenshots follow from the figure index.
The index is part of the export (Chapter 16.5).

qa: Where do the images in the Quick Guides come from?
Currently they are drawn process images; screenshots are added from the figure index.
May I use a screenshot from the production system?
Only with test data or fully anonymized and with approval (Chapter 16.1).
How do I report an outdated figure?
Via the clarification register with figure number and release (Appendix F).

title: Appendix H.1: Knowledge Checks and Solutions
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix H.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **knowledge checks** test understanding per chapter with questions on process, roles and status; the **solutions** explain the correct answer with a chapter reference. This guide shows their use in **training** and **self-study**.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Structure
bullets: Questions per chapter with difficulty level
Question types: multiple choice, matching, case example
Solutions with rationale and chapter reference

steps: Read the chapter and Quick Guide before starting the **knowledge check**.
Answer the questions **without aids**; case examples refer to the practical examples in Appendix I.1.
Compare with the **solutions** and read the rationale with **chapter reference**.

right.text: ~~Knowledge checks do not replace an authorization.~~ Access to oneSCM is granted via ALICE (Chapter 2.3), regardless of the training result.

steps: Review the chapter sections for questions answered incorrectly.
Trainers document the result as **training evidence** (Chapter 17.4).

bullets: Access to the knowledge checks (handbook or training material)
Time for about ten questions per chapter
Questions are reviewed with each release (Chapter 22.3).
Local variants of the questions exist per market (Chapter 20).
Solutions contain no personal sample data (Chapter 16.1).

qa: How many questions does a knowledge check have?
About ten per chapter, depending on the chapter's scope.
Is there a minimum score?
The market sets this for its training (Chapter 17.4).
Can I repeat the knowledge check?
Yes, as often as you like; it serves as a self-check.
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

title: Appendix I.1: Practical Examples along the Contract Process
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix I.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **practical examples** walk through end-to-end cases from **quote** to **termination**: business customer with collective invoice, private customer with e-signature, KAM-managed key account with special case, tyre contract. This guide shows how to **follow** the examples and use them in **training**.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Examples
bullets: Example 1: Business customer, collective invoice, signature by e-mail
Example 2: Private customer, e-signature via QR code
Example 3: KAM-managed key account with special case request

steps: Select the **example** that matches your role and customer group.
Carry out the steps in the **training system** with the specified **test data** (Appendix I.3).
At each **checkpoint**, compare your status with the status documented in the example.

right.text: ~~Run practical examples only in the training or test system.~~ In the production system, real applications are created and reviewed by Customer Management.

steps: In case of deviations, check the chapter and clarification register; report new deviations (Appendix F).
Use the examples for **knowledge checks** (Appendix H) and calculation examples (Appendix I.2).

bullets: ☐  Run with test data in the training system
Example 1 corresponds to the case in the Vans template "Application creation and management".
Division differences are marked in the examples (Chapter 21).
Checkpoints correspond to the checklists in Appendix B.

qa: Which example suits Vans dealers?
Example 1 (business customer) and Example 2 (private customer), both with Vans identifiers.
Are there examples of rejections?
Yes, Example 3 contains a special case request with rejection and resubmission.
Where does the test data come from?
From the test data catalog in Appendix I.3.

title: Appendix I.2: Calculation Examples and Finance Reference
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix I.2 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **calculation examples** show how **price, payment interval, term and mileage** affect the payment plan, **final settlement** and **refund**, and how **discounts and campaigns** take effect. This guide explains the examples step by step.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Examples
bullets: Term and mileage: effect on the price
Campaign and dealer discount in the quote
Early termination: final settlement and refund

sections.head: Finance reference
bullets: Price components and Cost Unit Split (Chapter 14.14)
Posting in NEMESIS, payment via MPay (Chapter 19)

steps: Read the example's **input data**: product, term, mileage, payment interval.
Follow the **payment plan**: total price, number and amount of installments, due dates.
Apply the **campaign or discount** and check the effect on the payment plan.

right.text: ~~The calculation examples use sample prices.~~ Only the market's price version and the price information from oneSCM are binding.

steps: Recalculate the **final settlement** for early termination: used share, refund, correction (Chapter 11.6).
Compare your result with the **price information** (PDF) from the system (Chapter 5.6).

bullets: **Dealer**: explain payment plan and price information
Product and configuration of the sample contract
The payment interval can later only be changed to "one-off" (Chapter 6).
Refunds are handled by the Finance department (Chapter 11.6).
Factor limits and clusters are described in Chapter 14.9.

qa: Why does my result differ from the price information?
Check price version, campaign conditions and rounding rules; in case of doubt, the system applies.
How is the refund calculated?
Pro rata by term and mileage per Chapter 11.6; the example shows the steps.
Does the example apply to Cars and Vans?
The calculation logic does; prices differ per division (Chapter 21.3).
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers
